qt: to the Commission João Oliveira (The Left) Subject:

The European Commission has imposed a restructuring process on TAP that has led to a reduction in its activity, restrictions on its number of aircraft and employees, and the sellingoff of strategic sections of the company to multinationals. This process of monopolistic concentration at European level, promoted by the European Commission, seeks to go as far as possible in delivering to the great European capital the tools that are strategic to the sovereignty and development of the Member States, running counter to the interests of their peoples. The Portuguese Government has now announced the sale of part of TAP’s capital to Lufthansa, with a shareholders’ agreement that will give the minority shareholder effective control of the company. In similar situations, we have seen the emergence of impositions – put there by the entity imposing the concentration but which then becomes concerned about competition – that led to the companies sold shrinking in terms of in aircraft, employees, slots or destinations. This was the case, for example, for ITA Airways, Swissair and Austrian Airlines. In view of the above: Could TAP be the victim of a similar process – originating in the European institutions – of being forced to reduce its activity/size following its sale to Lufthansa?
